refined_prompt: Create a curated bootstrap dataset of 50–100 historical and contemporary authorities in economics, investment, risk management, and central banking. Serve as seed data for Tomorrow's advisory context layer. Output a valid JSON array with schema: {id, name, role, birth_year, death_year?, country_of_origin, primary_field, summary, source, source_url, added_date, nobel_prize_year?, aum_billions?, institution?}. Store in data/authorities/roster_v1.0.json. Verify against acceptance criteria: no duplicates, all required fields present, role values in [economist|investor|risk_manager|central_banker], dates ISO 8601 or YYYY integers. Include 10 spot-check verifications against Wikipedia. Write Zod schema in data/authorities/schema.ts and 20+ test cases in tests/data/authorities.spec.ts. All entries must meet at least one tier: (1) Nobel Prize + Fields Medal, (2) top-20 university tenure OR direct policy leadership (Fed chair, World Bank chief), or (3) 5+ high-impact publications (>1000 Google Scholar citations). Inclusion criteria rationale: these four roles represent decision-makers and thought leaders in risk/finance; the roster enriches risk narratives with historical precedent and credibility signals, not hiring/advisory matching.
resolutions: Laureate definition: Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences (1969–present) + Fields Medal (mathematical economics). Excludes other honors to avoid scope creep.

Great investor/risk manager metrics: Three-tier inclusion (meet any one): (1) top-20 university tenure OR policy leadership, (2) $10B+ AUM or transformational institution, (3) 5+ high-impact publications. Balances rigor, market impact, and intellectual influence.
Data source: Wikipedia curated lists (primary) + IDEAS/RePEc + academic department websites. Manual v1 curation (~80 entries); future v2 adds async polling.

JSON schema: Minimal viable with required fields (id, name, role, birth_year, country_of_origin, primary_field, summary, source, added_date) and optional domain-specific fields (nobel_prize_year, aum_billions, institution, death_year). TypeScript interface + Zod validator.
Example shape: Concrete 3-entry examples provided (Krugman, Volcker, Dalio) showing all field types and role variations.
Scope rationale: All four roles are decision-makers in risk/finance domain. Roster is advisory context layer for narratives, NOT a hiring directory.
Dataset type: Bootstrap seed (v1.0, 50–100 entries). No auto-refresh in v1; manual curation + PR review. Versioning via v1.1, v2.0 for schema changes.

Integration context: Consumer is server/api/risk/enrich.ts for optional authority lookup to attach credibility signals (historical precedent, Taleb's fragility principle, Volcker precedent) to risk narratives.

Acceptance criteria: 50–100 entries, no duplicates, all required fields valid, role distribution ≥15 economists/10 investors/8 risk managers/7 central bankers, 10 spot-check verifications, 20+ test cases, zero schema violations.
File paths: data/authorities/roster_v1.0.json (dataset), data/authorities/schema.ts (Zod validator), tests/data/authorities.spec.ts (unit tests), data/authorities/README.md (consumer API guide).
confidence_rationale: High confidence because: (1) Ambiguities resolved via concrete, measurable definitions (Nobel Prize is objective; three-tier metrics are verifiable; 50–100 entry cap is bounded). (2) Schema is pragmatic—minimal required fields, optional domain-specific fields, example entries validate against it. (3) Acceptance criteria are testable and objective (no duplicates, required fields present, role enum compliance, spot-check verifications). (4) Integration context grounded in Tomorrow's risk narrative architecture. (5) Roadmap is realistic (7–10 days curation, 3–5 days schema/tests, 2–3 days QA). Caveat: 0.08 discount due to lack of direct Tomorrow codebase review—file paths (data/authorities/, server/api/risk/enrich.ts) are inferred from PLOEH bridge docs and standard project layout; may need adjustment if directory structure differs.
